name: Spontaneous Speech Variables
description: The achievements of Large Language Models in Natural Language Processing, especially for high-resource languages, call for a better understanding of their characteristics from a cognitive perspective. Researchers have attempted to evaluate artificial models by testing their ability to predict behavioral (e.g., eye-tracking fixations) and physiological (e.g., brain responses) variables during language processing (e.g., reading/listening). In this paper, we propose using spontaneous speech corpora to derive production variables (speech reductions, prosodic prominences) and applying them in a similar fashion. More precisely, we extract. We then test models trained with a standard procedure on different pretraining datasets (written, spoken, and mixed genres) for their ability to predict these two variables. reputation: A specialized cognitive/linguistic evaluation setup with limited adoption outside research on speech processing and model interpretability.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark based on predicting production variables from spontaneous speech; likely small and domain-specific, with results often reported via correlation or related regression metrics.
